cards.text: Some visitors come to Jesus: Pharisees and scribes, religious leaders and teachers of the law, who came all the way from Jerusalem. They've got a question for Jesus about His disciples. Friend, when people travel that far just to ask you one question, it is NOT a compliment question.

cards.question: The Pharisees and scribes say Jesus' disciples break the tradition of the elders. What are the disciples doing?

answers.text: They don't wash their hands before they eat
They don't fast twice a week like others
They don't pray three times every day

cards.question: The Pharisees and scribes asked why the disciples break the tradition of the elders. Jesus answers with a question of His own. What does He ask them?

answers.text: Why they break God's command for their tradition
Why they came all this way to ask about hands
Why they never wash their own hands either

cards.text: Then Jesus goes straight to what God said: 'Honor your father and mother' and 'Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.'

But Jesus says their teaching goes another way. If someone tells his father or mother, 'Whatever you would have received from me is a gift devoted to God,' then their tradition says something about him.

cards.question: In the Pharisees' teaching, a man tells his parents that whatever they would have received from him is a gift devoted to God. Their tradition says he still has to honor his parents with it. True or false?
Jesus sums up what their tradition does: they ___ the word of God for the sake of their ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus doesn't soften it one bit: 'You hypocrites!' They came to talk about hands, and now THEY'RE the ones getting looked at.

cards.question: Jesus says one of Israel's prophets saw these Pharisees and scribes coming: the prophet ___ prophesied correctly about them.

cards.text: Isaiah was one of Israel's prophets, and Jesus says Isaiah got these leaders right. Isaiah's words are about two things: lips and hearts.

cards.question: In the words from Isaiah that Jesus quotes, these people honor God with their lips. Where are their hearts?
In the words from Isaiah that Jesus quotes, God says the worship of these people is worth a lot to Him. True or false?

cards.text: God says, 'They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.' Big words, far-off heart: that's signing the office birthday card 'Love you SO much!' for a guy whose name you had to read off the envelope.
Then Jesus calls the crowd to Him and says, 'Listen and understand.' Friend, that's TWO jobs. On a good day I'm good for one.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd what really defiles a man. What does He say defiles him?

answers.text: What comes out of his mouth

cards.text: Then the disciples come to Jesus with an update about the Pharisees.

cards.question: The disciples tell Jesus the Pharisees were pleased when they heard His teaching about what defiles a man. True or false?

cards.text: Jesus answers with a picture: 'Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.'

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples to disregard the Pharisees. He calls them ___ guides.
Jesus says if a blind man leads a blind man, only the one leading falls into a pit. True or false?

cards.text: Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, says, 'Explain this parable to us.'

cards.question: Peter asks Jesus to explain the parable. Before explaining, Jesus asks the disciples a question. What does He ask?

answers.text: Why they told Him about the Pharisees
If the crowd had understood it

cards.question: Jesus explains the first half of the parable. According to Jesus, where does whatever enters the mouth go?

answers.text: Into the stomach and then out
Into the heart and stays there
Into the mind and changes it

cards.question: Jesus says the things that come out of the mouth come from the ___, and these things defile a man.
Jesus names what comes out of the heart. Which of these is on His list?

cards.text: Here's the whole list Jesus gives: evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony and slander. Not one thing on that list ever came off a dirty hand.

cards.question: Jesus brings it back to where the Pharisees and scribes started. He says eating with unwashed hands defiles a man. True or false?

findings.problem: The joke says they traveled that far 'just to ask you one question.' Matthew 15:1 says only that they came from Jerusalem and asked. It never gives a reason for the trip, so 'just to ask' adds a purpose the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'Jesus sums up what their tradition does.' That puts the word 'tradition' on screen, which gives away the second blank and rules out 'family' and 'temple.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 9 already said that Isaiah is one of Israel's prophets and that he prophesied correctly about them. This card says the same thing again and adds only 'lips and hearts.' It is mostly a recap.
The statement says the disciples 'tell Jesus' about the Pharisees. In Matthew 15:12 the disciples ask Him a question: 'Are You aware that the Pharisees were offended...'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to fill in the wording 'blind guides' with no setup to reason from. The wrong answers 'hired' and 'young' don't fit any picture already given, so 'blind' stands out or the baker has to guess. It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: In the same scene, Mark 7:22 has Jesus list 'greed' and 'envy,' along with 'arrogance' and 'foolishness,' which are close to 'Pride and folly.' A baker who knows Mark could argue that both wrong answers are on Jesus' list.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The punchline 'Not one thing on that list ever came off a dirty hand' comes right before card 14, which asks whether eating with unwashed hands defiles a man. The joke gives away that answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Story cards 3, 5 and 8 are flat narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 3 is 'Then the disciples come to Jesus with an update about the Pharisees.' Cards 5 and 8 are bare quotes. This stop reads like a summary, not his storytelling.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
